item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-EVERTON-CHELSEA - AFP Jack Grealish has officially returned to training at Finch Farm as he looks to put a difficult period at Everton behind him. The 31-year-old playmaker is now targeting a Premier League return following the international break, having missed the Toffees' most recent outings due to a combination of fitness issues and internal disciplinary measures. Path to first-team reintegration at Finch Farm Everton have confirmed that Grealish is back on the grass at their Finch Farm training base, signaling the beginning of his reintegration into the senior setup. The creative midfielder has been following a tailored individual program to regain his sharpness after a period on the sidelines. The club’s medical and coaching staff have designed a plan that should see Grealish rejoin full first-team sessions early next week, providing a significant boost to David Moyes’ options ahead of a crucial winter period in the Premier League. While the atmosphere at Everton has been tense following recent results, the return of a player with Grealish's technical quality is seen as a necessary step forward. The veteran attacker has only managed six appearances this season during his second loan spell on Merseyside, struggling to find the consistency that previously made him a fan favorite. Despite the optimism surrounding his return to training, he remains unavailable for the immediate home fixture against Coventry City. The target for his competitive comeback has been set for the trip to the Gtech Community Stadium on November 23, where Everton will face a resilient Brentford side. item.title: Red Sox News & Links: Will the Sox trade Franklin Arias this offseason?
item.description: BINGHAMTON, NY - MAY 26: Franklin Arias #50 of the Portland Sea Dogs celebrates with teammates after defeating the Binghamton Rumble Ponies at Mirabito Stadium on Tuesday, May 26, 2026 in Binghamton, New York. (Photo by Kylie Richelle/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) As Matt laid out yesterday, there sure are a lot of rumors involving the Red Sox and shortstops, despite the fact that Franklin Arias is a shortstop with nothing left to prove in AAA. So what does that say about how the Sox view Arias? Maybe it doesn’t say anything than that they’re doing their due diligence. But here’s what the current dean of the Red Sox beat says about it in his offseason preview piece: “Some in the organization view Arias as almost untouchable. In a poor positional free agent class, however, the Sox are unlikely to keep Arias off-limits in trade talks, but they’d only consider dealing him for a star with multiple years of control.” (Alex Speier, Boston Globe) Meanwhile, another Red Sox beat reporter thinks a big trade isn’t that likely this offseason. “Breslow has gone down the trade road a lot in his three previous offseasons as chief baseball officer. With the prospect haul that was sent to the Orioles for Adley Rutschman, this could be the year free agency is the option Breslow explores the most. Randy Arozarena, to me, would be the perfect fit in the middle of the batting order.” (Ian Browne, MLB.com) Amidst the relatively disappointing start of the “Big Three Era” (remember when it was briefly the “Big Four”?) it’s understandable that many fans harbor some scepticism about prospects like Arias. But it’s hardly time to close the book on Roman Anthony, who, through all the injuries, still showed plenty of signs of future stardom in 2026. (Brian Murphy, MLB.com) Hopefully a full offseason of rest is enough for Anthony to put his wrist injuries behind him. If so, maybe he’ll appear on the list of Silver Slugger finalists next year. As it stands the Sox landed two players on that list: Willson Contreras and Wilyer Abreu, neither of whom has won the award before. (Tim Healey, Boston Globe) But will Anthony, Contreras, and Abreu get any help in the lineup? Here’s a look at a few free agent names who might be a good fit for the Sox, starting with Seiya Suzuki. (Jen McCaffrey, The Athletic) The Sox did actually make a significant signing yesterday, though not of the player personnel variety. Shelley Duncan, who, like Chad Tracy, has spent years as a AAA manager, has been added to Tracy’s big league coaching staff. (Sean McAdam, Chris Cotillo, MassLive)

item.title: LeBron James Shrinks Scoring Role For 76ers Defense
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James is taking fewer shots than ever before in his long career, yet the Philadelphia 76ers are winning more games than any other team in the league. Through his first seven games, the four-time champion is averaging 15.7 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 7.4 assists. His field-goal attempts have dropped to just 13.1 per game, while his free-throw attempts sit at 4.4. These numbers mark the lowest pace for his scoring average and shot volume since he entered the NBA as a rookie. Instead of carrying the offense alone, James is now playing as a facilitator alongside a roster packed with elite scorers. On Wednesday night, Detroit Pistons fell 112-106 as the 76ers secured eight wins from their opening nine contests. This surprising drop in personal usage has allowed Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown to generate offense independently while James directs the flow. Defense Becomes the Team Identity While James cuts back on his scoring, the starting five has limited opponents’ scoring. The group has held teams to just 95.4 points per 100 possessions across their first five games together. For context, the league’s best defense before Thursday was allowing 103 points per 100 possessions. This gap shows how much the Sixers have improved on that end of the floor. James made the goal clear after the win over Detroit. After defeating the Pistons on Wednesday, “Our defense is going to be our identity,” James stated, according to NBC News . The starting lineup features James, Brown, Maxey, V.J. Edgecombe, and Joel Embiid, a group that combines for 36 All-Star selections. They have outscored opponents by 15 points in 77 minutes of play together. Cleveland Returns With a Different Star James faces his old team, the Cleveland Cavaliers, for the first time since choosing Philadelphia in free agency. During 11 Cleveland seasons, he guided the franchise to its initial 2016 NBA championship. The Cavaliers enter Friday with a 4-4 record after back-to-back losses to Oklahoma City. They also face injury concerns with key player Jarrett Allen listed as questionable for tonight’s game. Donovan Mitchell has averaged 22.5 points for Cleveland, but the team needs better collective production to beat Philadelphia. James Harden has struggled with his shooting efficiency. With the Eastern Conference’s top record, the 76ers have claimed five straight victories. James noted that his role has changed because he knows the team needs him to be ready for late-game situations. Patience Over Hype Despite the strong start, James warns against looking too far ahead at the end of the season. Regarding this talented group, certain fans propose an NBA Finals appearance is inevitable. item.title: ‘Looks play a big part’: Former WNBA star explains why Sophie Cunningham is popular despite lackluster stats
item.description: Aug 23, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) reacts while warming up prior to a game against the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Caitlin Clark has become the face of the WNBA, and the Indiana Fever have become one of the league’s most popular teams because of her. But WNBA legend Angel McCoughtry thinks Clark’s teammate Kelsey Mitchell isn’t getting nearly enough credit. Appearing on the Get To The Point podcast with Terrell Owens and Chris Spencer, McCoughtry argued that looks play a bigger role in WNBA marketing than they do in other sports. She pointed to Mitchell as an example, saying that the Fever’s “best player” is barely recognized by fans. Mitchell’s Big Season Mitchell put together a terrific season for the Fever in 2026. She led the team in scoring, averaging 24.7 points per game, while Clark averaged 22.3 points per game. Mitchell has also been one of Indiana’s most consistent players in recent years, earning All-Star honors and serving as the Fever’s top scoring threat alongside Clark. Still, Clark is the one who draws the crowds and the endorsements. Her arrival turned the Fever into a national draw, and she has become one of the most marketable athletes in sports. ‘Looks play a big part’ McCoughtry, a five-time WNBA All-Star, said that she noticed the gap in attention firsthand. “In the NFL and NBA, if you’re good, you’re good. In the WNBA, if you look pretty… You might not be the best player…” McCoughtry said. “I went to a conference, and everybody loved Indiana. They love Caitlin Clark. I said, ‘How many of you know Kelsey Mitchell?’ None of them raised their hand. She’s the best player on the team,” McCoughtry said, on the podcast . “The leading scorer on that team. Only 100k. She don’t have a million followers.” Owens jumped in to ask if McCoughtry was suggesting that Clark is pretty. She declined to say that she was, but she then brought up Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, pointing out that she has an Adidas shoe deal despite averaging “nine points per game.” Cunningham actually averaged 7.9 points per game this season. McCoughtry said that there are other girls that are “balling” that don’t have similar deals. “Not the best player you’ve ever seen, but she’s getting the brand endorsements,” McCoughtry said. “In the woman’s game, is it really about how good you are or the visibility – how pretty you are?” “Yes, looks play a part. They play a big part,” McCoughtry said. Spencer went on to bring up other examples like Anna Kournikova and Michelle Wei, who weren’t the most successful in their sport but received brand sponsorships, potentially because of their looks. item.title: Gateway Dirt Nationals Best Appearing Car Contest Returns In 2026 With Cash Prizes
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The 2026 Gateway Dirt Nationals will give fans a direct say in which race cars look the best on the track. Organizers confirmed that the Best Appearing Car Contest returns this year for both the Super Late Model and Modified divisions. Two drivers will walk away with cash prizes, and the crowd gets to pick the winners. FloRacing and the event organizers plan to hand out $1,000 to the winner in each division. The money might seem small compared to the race purse, but the bragging rights are worth much more to the teams. Tyler Carpenter won the Super Late Model title in 2026, while Haleigh Gross took the award in the Modified class, according to FloRacing . Now the competition resets for a new year of paint jobs and creative designs. A Decade of Indoor Racing The race takes place inside The Dome at America’s Center, a venue that has hosted the event for ten years. This setting allows for unique paint schemes that might not survive on outdoor tracks. Drivers and teams arrive each December with eye-catching designs to grab the attention of the crowd. The contest celebrates this decade of racing indoors by rewarding the teams that put the most effort into their look. They will select 10 cars from each division to become finalists before the public votes. This step ensures that only the most impressive rides make it to the final round. Photo galleries featuring all 20 finalists will appear on FloRacing so fans can see the details up close. How the Voting Works Once the finalists are announced, the fans take control of the outcome. Supporters can visit FloRacing.com to cast their votes for their favorite cars. During the voting period, rules permit fans to cast up to four votes each day. This high volume of voting keeps the engagement high as the event gets closer. The specific dates for voting and other contest details will be released as the event approaches. FloRacing reported that the 2026 Kubota Gateway Dirt Nationals will bring Super Late Models and Modifieds indoors for three nights of racing in December. FloRacing will broadcast all three nights of racing live for viewers who cannot travel to St. Louis. A Massive Field of Drivers The race itself features a huge entry list that proves dirt racing is stronger than ever. The 2026 Gateway Dirt Nationals has 129 drivers entered in the Super Late Model division, according to a Monday verification by FloRacing. Rather than a small regional race, this gathering brings together the best dirt racers in the country. The field includes defending champion Bobby Pierce, who is the first three-time winner of this event. Former champions including Brandon Sheppard, Tyler Carpenter, and Tyler Erb also appear on the list. The entry list resembles a roster of dirt racing royalty. item.title: NFL Rumors: Insider Sheds Light on Lamar Jackson’s Future with Baltimore Ravens
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered a severe thumb injury in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills in his first game back after missing multiple weeks with an ankle sprain. While Baltimore just acquired Jacoby Brissett to fill the void at quarterback for the rest of 2026, questions remain about Jackson’s future with the franchise. Baltimore must figure out something with Jackson this offseason. The 2027 NFL salary cap is currently projected by OverTheCap.com to be $327 million. Jackson’s cap hit next season is too high for the franchise to justify, especially given the needs throughout its roster with aspirations to rebound as a playoff contender. Lamar Jackson contract ( Spotrac ): $84.34 million cap hit in 2027, $42.47 million dead cap in 2028 Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta’s options are further complicated by the contract extension he signed his MVP quarterback to in 2023. Jackson’s five-year deal included a no-trade clause, meaning that Baltimore needs his explicit approval to move him to another club. The franchise also can’t use the franchise tag on him in 2028 when he expires. That gives Jackson, who doesn’t have an official agent, complete leverage over the situation. Many in sports media and around the National Football League have speculated that the two-time NFL MVP and the storied franchise could potentially part ways after the 2026 season. However, that doesn’t seem to be the plan. Ahead of Baltimore’s Week 8 Thursday Night Football matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars, NFL insider James Palmer reported on Amazon Prime Video that the Ravens are willing to make Jackson the highest-paid player in NFL history. When the Kansas City Chiefs reworked the Patrick Mahomes contract in June, the agreement added two years to his contract and made the average annual value a record-setting $64 million. Mahomes and Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott ($60 million AAV) are the only NFL players making $60-plus million per season. Ahead of his age-30 season, it stands to reason that Jackson would be looking for another five-year contract. Baltimore could tack four years onto his current deal, potentially at $65 million per season. It would make him the highest-paid player in NFL history, keep him under contract through his age-35 season and likely allow him to spend his entire career in a Ravens uniform. item.description: PHOENIX, AZ - AUGUST 22: Elly De La Cruz #44 of the Cincinnati Reds celebrates with teammate Sal Stewart #27 after hitting a home run in the fifth inning during the game between the Cincinnati Reds and the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field on Saturday, August 22, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Brendon Baranov/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Joey Votto was one of the greatest hitters of all time, let alone his own generation. He never once won a Silver Slugger Award. Jay Bruce, Votto’s longtime sidekick during the best run of form the Cincinnati Reds have had at any point during the last 35 years, won a pair of Silver Slugger Awards in his career. Silver Sluggers are not exactly the most precise way to define hitting excellence. That said, they still carry weight among the players themselves, however, as they are voted on among managers and coaches league-wide to determine which players were the ‘best’ hitters at their own positions during the most recent season. The finalists at each position in both the National League and American League were announced on Friday, and both of Cincinnati’s best hitters from 2026 were among them. The managers and coaches named Elly De La Cruz a finalist at the shortstop position, while Sal Stewart was named a finalist among the ‘Utility’ category. item.title: Tennessee’s key to beating Kentucky? Don’t beat yourself
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - SEPTEMBER 12: Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel talks with a referee during the college football game between the Tennessee Volunteers and the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on September 12th, 2026 at Bobby Dodd Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tennessee saw a golden opportunity to give themselves a cushion for the rest of the season two weeks ago in Columbia slip through their fingertips. The Volunteers found a way to lose against South Carolina as the mistakes finally caught up with them late. Tennessee was penalized 12 times for 90 yards against the Gamecocks, famously taking three passing touchdowns from George MacIntyre off the board. The penalties have been a theme for Tennessee ever since Josh Heupel arrived in Knoxville. Heupel’s Tennessee teams have finished outside of the top 100 overall in penalties in four of his five seasons. 2026 has been no different. The Volunteers rank 100th in FBS with 61 penalties on the year. They’re 91st in penalty yards, checking in with 62.12 yards surrendered per game. Tennessee’s opponent this week, Kentucky, is 17th in the same statistic. That’s been a theme for Kentucky all season long — playing clean and taking advantage of opportunities. It’s something that quarterback Kenny Minchey can hang his hat on this year, throwing 14 touchdowns against just one interception. Kentucky has a turnover margin of +13 for the season. Tennessee is +3 in that category for the season. The Volunteers have turned the ball over 11 times on the season, with an opportunistic, aggressive defense propping up their overall margin. Kentucky has turned the ball over just five times all season. “Playing a really good football team that is playing extremely well together,” Josh Heupel said of Kentucky. “You look at their ability to win multiple ways, finish games. Turnover margin, they’ve been elite. One of the least-penalized teams in the league, playing really smart all three phases, so it’ll be a great test.” With an inexperienced quarterback making just his fourth start, keeping things on schedule is a must. The little things — the 3rd and 3 that turns into 3rd and 8 — those are the things that Tennessee really can’t afford down the homestretch, starting on Saturday night. The Volunteers are playing a defensive, ball-control brand this season, and that brand really needs clean football to be successful. We’ll see if Tennessee can clean things up against Kentucky on Saturday. Kickoff is set for 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN.

item.title: Christian Pulisic’s New Deal Forever Links His Legacy to AC Milan
item.description: Christian Pulisic’s New Deal Forever Links His Legacy to AC Milan Christian Pulisic has signed a new contract that will keep him at AC Milan until 2031. It is a well-deserved renewal and a career-defining moment for the American winger. Christian Pulisic is staying put at AC Milan . The 28-year-old American winger will remain under contract with the Rossoneri until June 2031, earning a pay rise to €6.5 million net per year, with the figure potentially reaching €10 million if he achieves certain objectives. However you look at it, Pulisic is now one of AC Milan’s highest-paid players and among the top earners in Serie A , alongside Lautaro Martínez , Nicolò Barella, Kevin De Bruyne , and Kenan Yıldız . All of this comes on the heels of Gerry Cardinale, founder and managing partner of RedBird Capital Partners and owner of AC Milan since August 2022, telling CBS Sports: “We have a connection. We’re two guys from Pennsylvania trying to find our way and understand Italy. He’s Captain America, but he’s also my franchise player.” That is an important milestone for an American playing in Europe, particularly one who has already represented three major clubs. Today, Pulisic can look in the mirror and know that his career will be defined by his time at AC Milan, much like Clint Dempsey’s was defined by Fulham or Tim Howard’s by Everton . Pulisic is a Rossoneri player, and for American soccer, that is a remarkable achievement. Pulisic’s Numbers: Not Just Impressive, But a Benchmark The tale of the tape for Pulisic at AC Milan deserves a standing ovation at the San Siro : 45 goals and 28 assists in 144 games. He has also scored four goals against Inter in all competitions, which puts him ahead of Milan legends including Marco van Basten, George Weah, and Ronaldinho . At the UEFA Champions League level, Pulisic has scored five goals, one of which was an Olimpico against Club Brugge . His longest scoring streak has been four consecutive games, a run that included goals against Venezia , Inter and Lecce in Serie A, as well as a Champions League goal against Liverpool . With 45 goals to his name, his tally in Rossoneri stripes surpasses those of Oliver Bierhoff, Robinho, Ronaldinho, Andrea Pirlo , Stephan El Shaarawy, Roberto Donadoni, and Roberto Baggio . The only blemish on Pulisic’s statistics at Milan has been the lack of silverware, with the American having won just one Supercoppa Italiana during his four seasons at the club. That has not been entirely his fault, as Milan have gone through a huge coaching carousel during that period while struggling to find their identity and establish consistency. With Pulisic’s contract approaching its expiration before the renewal, one of the main talking points in Italy was that he could go down as a very good player whose time at the club would ultimately be remembered more for turmoil than success. item.description: Preview: Scott Parker prepares for second game in charge as West Ham travel to Blackburn After a stunning second-half comeback against Cardiff City midweek, West Ham travel to Lancashire to face Blackburn Rovers on Saturday. Scott Parker will take charge of his second game since becoming West Ham boss. Parker was in the dugout on Wednesday against Cardiff, despite only being announced and meeting the team for the first time on the morning of the game. West Ham fell 3-0 behind the Bluebirds in just 45 minutes, giving the new boss a tough task, but he rose to the challenge as the team turned the game around in the second half, scoring three goals to salvage a point. Blackburn fell to a second consecutive defeat in midweek as they were beaten 2-1 at home by Stoke City. This comes after they were beaten 4-0 last weekend by high-flying Swansea. The Hammers sit in eighth, one point inside the playoffs, while Blackburn sit in fourteenth place, five points behind the East London club. Rovers are set to be without Ryan Alebiosu, meaning Gady Beyuku could take his place in the right-back spot. As for the visitors, the only known doubt is Keiber Lamadrid, who continues to suffer from a knee injury. It remains to be seen which team Parker will select, as he has only been at the club for a couple of days, but with how the team played in the second half on Wednesday, it seems everyone involved in the comeback could be involved from the start. Ahead of Saturday’s fixture, which will see over 7,000 Hammers fans travel to East Lancashire, Parker spoke to the press. “As always, it’s going to be a tough game. I know they’re coming off a couple of bad results, but they’re a competitive team, with an experienced manager in Tony [Mowbray]. “We’re going to give the best versions of ourselves, and certainly try to build on that second half. item.description: FOXBOROUGH – Patriots offensive lineman Matt Pryor didn’t have NFL dreams. He didn’t even really want to play football. As a kid growing up in Long Beach, Pryor was too big to play Pop Warner due to being over the weight limit. It was his size, however, that caught the attention of a football coach at San Pedro High School. In the summer before his freshman year, Pryor accompanied his mother and cousin to football tryouts. Dressed like a typical teenager from Southern California, he stood by the field wearing Dickies, a polo shirt and a pair of Chuck Taylors. That’s when the coach spotted the massive kid observing. “Chilling. Watching my cousin try out. Coach sees me from the field, and is like, ‘Hey, you want to play?’ I’m like, nah, man, I’m good.’” That’s when his mother, Brandi Calandrino, stepped in. “And my mom was like, ‘nah, get out there,” Pryor said. “She goes, ‘I ain’t paying for you to go to school. Shout out to my mom for making me get out there. Once I started playing I fell in love with it. But, yeah, definitely did not see myself being where I am right now.” RELATED : Early data projections: Pats look to keep momentum in Week 9 showdown vs. Packers Pryor, who’s 6-foot-7 and weighs 332 pounds, certainly looks the part of a future NFL offensive lineman. After starting on the Arizona Cardinals practice squad, the Patriots signed Pryor to their active roster in October after a series of injuries to their guard position. item.title: Paderborn vs. Eintracht Frankfurt preview: Die Adler searching for third successive win
item.description: Paderborn vs. Eintracht Frankfurt preview: Die Adler searching for third successive win Paderborn Competing in the top flight for the first time since 2019-20, Paderborn are sitting in 14th spot after winning two, drawing three and losing three of their eight league games. The second of those victories came in their most recent home outing, a 1-0 success over Hamburger SV on October 24. However, they have failed to score since Rayan Philippe netted an 88th-minute winner against Hamburg. They fell to a 1-0 defeat to Stuttgart in the DFB-Pokal, before they played out a goalless draw in last Saturday’s away clash against Borussia Mönchengladbach. While the goals have dried up, Paderborn can at least be pleased with the fact they have avoided defeat in each of their last three league games (W1, D2). However, the league’s second-lowest scorers know they will need to improve in the final third if they are to put distance between themselves and the drop zone, with Ralf Kettemann’s side currently sitting two points clear of the bottom three. They can take some confidence from the fact they have won all three of their previous home meetings with Frankfurt, even if the most recent of those encounters took place nearly seven years ago in December 2019. Team News Mario Götze is unlikely to feature due to an ear infection, denying him the chance to face off against his brother Felix Götze. Hütter is also without Jessic Ngankam, while Robin Koch is a doubt due to a knee problem. Eintracht Frankfurt Frankfurt head into the weekend in eighth spot after winning three, drawing two and losing three of their eight Bundesliga matches. Die Adler took maximum points from last Sunday’s home clash against Hamburger SV, just a matter of days after beating the same opponent by the same 3-1 scoreline in the DFB-Pokal. The league encounter was level at one goal apiece at half time before Raphael Onyedika and Younes Ebnoutalib found the net to fire Adi Hütter’s side to all three points. After enjoying a successful outing at Deutsche Bank Park, Frankfurt will now head on their travels with the minimum objective of avoiding a third consecutive away defeat in the Bundesliga. Their ultimate goal will be to record their second away win of the season, although that would require them to beat Paderborn at the Home Deluxe Arena for the very first time. While a head-to-head away win has evaded them up until this point, they were victorious in the most recent meeting between the two sides in June 2020, when they held off a Paderborn fightback to clinch a 3-2 win. Team News The visitors are expected to be without Marcel Hoffmeier, Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant and Timur Gayret. In positive news, Sven Michel is available for selection after recovering from the injury that has kept him out of the last two matches.

item.title: Shedeur Sanders bristles at reporter after being asked about hiring an agent mid-season
item.description: Oct 1, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) practices before the game at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders is in line to make his first start of the season on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints, as Deshaun Watson has been placed in the concussion protocol after suffering a helmet-to-helmet hit in last weekend’s loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, which dropped the Browns to 5-3 on the season and saw them cede first place in the AFC North to the Steelers. Sanders, who is in his second season with the Browns after being drafted in the fifth round in 2025, recently hired Adie von Gontard, CEO of Young Money APAA Sports, as his agent, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The hire led to speculation that Sanders may be looking to maneuver his way out of Cleveland via trade following Watson’s strong start to the season, which has cemented the veteran’s job as the starter. An NFL reporter asked Sanders about the decision to seek representation during Wednesday’s media availability. Sanders, however, bristled at the question, wanting to know how it was relevant to this weekend’s game against New Orleans. “What that got to do with this game?” Sanders asked. “I’m focused on this game. Anything else really don’t matter at this point.” Shedeur Sanders asked why he hired an agent #Browns https://t.co/P5kRMLgzbo — Daryl Ruiter (@RuiterWrongFAN) November 4, 2026 Although hiring an agent mid-season doesn’t specifically relate to Sunday’s game, it’s a more than fair question to ask a quarterback, especially ahead of what could be a career-altering start. It’s just as fair for Sanders to want to keep the focus on preparing for the Saints, although he might’ve benefited from approaching the situation with a bit more tact. For what it’s worth, Shedeur Sanders, who had a somewhat contentious relationship with Cleveland media in his rookie season, made his stance on the media entering this season clear during training camp. “I don’t think there’s anything negative about it, but I don’t really like when people have platforms and don’t use it for the right reasons,” Sanders told Kevin Clark of the media criticism he’s received NFL quarterback. “I don’t respect it. So, it’s like, things I don’t respect, I don’t give my time to.” The young quarterback has been proactive about trying to improve his relationship with the media this season, but at times just can’t seem to get out of his own way. item.description: (Photo by Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images At some point, somebody at the DFB needs to sit Germany’s best young footballers down and explain that moving to England is not a mandatory career milestone. Seriously. Can we stop doing this? Germany keeps producing ridiculously talent ed players, only to watch them head to the Premier League, where their careers sometimes turn into expensive exercises in frustration . Need examples? Glad you asked. Timo Werner went to Chelsea after establishing himself as one of Europe’s most dangerous forward s at RB Leipzig. He won the Champions League, but his confidence and goalscoring consistency never recovered to the same level. He was mock ed by the media, chided by fans, a nd pummeled on social media into becoming nothing more than a meme. His subsequent return to Leipzig did not restore his former standing, and he eventually found himself rebuilding his career in MLS. Kai Havertz is perhaps the most frustrating example. Arsenal still seems fascinated by the player they believe he can become rather than the player he actually is. He is a useful, versatile footballer, but the idea that he is some elite attacking superstar needs to be retired. He has consistently underwhelmed f or Germany, too, and his performances rarely justify the expectations surrounding him. Yet coaches keep trying to unlock something that might not actually be there. Florian Wirtz was arguably the best player in Germany before moving to Liverpool. Now he is struggling to reproduce that extraordinary Baye r Leverkusen form consistently. The talent has not disappeared, but perhaps there is a lesson in leaving a system where you are thrivin g. And Nick Woltemade? Another enormous talent who has moved to England and suddenly finds himself fighting to establish his place and rediscover his b est form… at Juventus, while on loan from Newcastle United. The Magpies spent a fortune on Woltemade and could not eve n stomach keeping him on the roster for the second year of his contract… yikes! There is nothing inherently wrong with the Premier League. It is an excellent competition. But England is not the promised land, and a bigger transfer fee does not automatically mean a better career. Amid all of their WR injury issues, it should come as little surprise that Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated revealed the 49ers are open to adding WR help, with a link to Indianapolis Colts WR Josh Downs as a potential option. 49ers linked to trade for Josh Downs amid WR injury issues "Downs is one of a number of receivers on the market, with the Chiefs and Steelers among the teams looking for help at the position," Breer writes. "And the Niners are open to adding, too, though with improving health there, they're less desperate than they were a couple of weeks ago." While this link to Downs isn't very strong, this report on the 49ers' trade deadline plans does point to some WR help being a potential option for San Francisco. But with Demarcus Robinson set to come back for the 49ers in Week 9, and the potential for both Evans and Samuel to return to the field, it wouldn't be surprising to see the 49ers pass on spending meaningful capital on WR help. But Breer's report indicates the 49ers are showing some interest in WR help, with Downs one of the more realistic options for John Lynch this season. Will they actually add a WR like Downs?
